- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) or trending negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is rising, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >+2% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.2–0.6), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day sentiment trend, not historical momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 1–2% below forecast, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 30 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
